items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good countdown geography video for BHUGOL, a popular geography fun-facts YouTube channel: five countries you can drive across in about an hour. The Narrator is thrilled to be telling you this: enthusiastic, upbeat, bright and very expressive, like an excited friend who can't wait to show you something amazing. Big smile in the voice the whole way. Wide, lively pitch movement: punch each 'Number five', 'Number four'... like a game-show reveal, and make 'And number one: The Gambia.' the biggest reveal of all. Rise with real curiosity on every question, give a tiny comic pause before each punchline ('you'll need a boat.', '...and just drive in.', 'That's sideways.'), and say every number with genuine amazement. The first line 'You can drive across this entire country in 25 minutes.' is a bold, surprising claim. The last line 'So, fastest to cross? Gambia. But a whole country, end to end...' trails off with the voice staying up, mid-thought, so it can loop straight back into the first line. Pace is quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, with short crisp pauses; never slow, flat, calm, sleepy or documentary-serious. Accent: native General American English narrator, neutral American accent from the first word to the last. VOICE IDENTITY: always the same warm baritone host, same person and same energy level from the first line to the last. Read numbers naturally: '2,000' as 'two thousand', '27' as 'twenty-seven', '43' as 'forty-three', '6 million' as 'six million'. Pronounce 'Andorra' as 'an-DOR-uh', 'Liechtenstein' as 'LIK-ten-shtine', 'Gambia' as 'GAM-bee-uh', 'Malta' as 'MAWL-tuh'.
lines: You can drive across this entire country in 25 minutes.
Here are 5 countries you can drive across in about an hour. One is a trick.
Number five: Andorra, wedged between France and Spain.
Border to border, about 45 kilometres, climbing past 2,000 metres.
The main island is just 27 kilometres long. Tip to tip, under an hour.
Drive any further, and you'll need a boat.
One expressway crosses the whole country: 43 kilometres, about 40 minutes.
A country of 6 million people, done before your podcast ends.
Yep, the country from the start: 25 kilometres, about 25 minutes.
It doesn't even have an airport. You land next door... and just drive in.
Cross it here, and it takes about 20 minutes.
The trick? That's sideways. Lengthwise, the road runs over 400 kilometres.
So, fastest to cross? Gambia. But a whole country, end to end...
